paper.title: Obesity and Dyslipidemia in South Asians

audience_doubt: Is it even for me? Is my BMI telling me the truth?
message: BMI alone can flatter an Indian body, so ask for your waist and body composition too.
reasoning: People with a 'normal' BMI assume they are fine, or that treatment is not for them. Showing the two BMI scales side by side makes 'built for Indian biology' visible in three seconds, and the waist flags give a number they can check at home before they talk to a doctor.

carousel.caption:
Your BMI says 'normal'. Your waist may disagree.

Studies find South Asians tend to carry more body fat at the same BMI than white Caucasians, and health risks can show up at lower BMI and waist measurements. That is why Asian Indian guidance draws the lines lower: BMI from 23 for overweight, and a waist of 80 cm (women) or 90 cm (men) as the flag for abdominal obesity.

These are screening flags, not a diagnosis. A doctor reads them alongside your labs.

steerclub.com

Source: Nutrients 2013;5(7):2708, Obesity and Dyslipidemia in South Asians.
carousel.caption_hi:
Aapka BMI kehta hai 'normal'. Kamar shayad na kahe.

Studies batati hain ki South Asians mein same BMI par body fat zyada ho sakta hai. Isliye Asian Indian guidance mein lines neeche hain: overweight BMI 23 se, aur kamar 80 cm (mahila) ya 90 cm (purush).

Ye screening flags hain, diagnosis nahi. Doctor aapke labs ke saath padhte hain.

steerclub.com

Source: Nutrients 2013;5(7):2708.
